Hi Alex - great to meet you and the team earlier. Recap + recommended next steps below. I cc'd Rishi (our performance lead) for any deeper perf tuning.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Target: P95 <= 200ms (streamed), P50 ~ 60-80ms; 150 QPS steady, bursts to 300 QPS, ~50 concurrent sessions.
- Avg token length: ~120 tokens. Streaming required.

Recommended initial config to hit SLOs (ballpark):
1) Model variant: run a quantized 3-4B variant in the pilot and compare to a 7B producing option for quality headroom. Example: use "redwood-3b-quant" (int8) as baseline, fall back to "redwood-7b" for higher-quality flows.
2) Continuous batching: enable small, time-window batching (10-25ms) + size cap to avoid tail latency spikes - this reduces per-token cost while respecting streaming latency.
3) KV/prefix caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (support chat context caching) - often reduces tokenscompute for repeated system prompts by 15-30%.
4) Quantization profile: start with int8 (native runtime support) - typical perf improvement ~1.8-2.5x over fp16 with minimal quality delta. Consider int4 for non-critical flows after a small eval for potential 3-4x perf gains but with higher risk to nuanced outputs.
5) Concurrency and routing: provision a pool sized for your concurrency (start with capacity for 60 concurrent sessions) with smart routing (latency-first) and autoscale burst to handle 300 QPS short bursts.
6) Streaming optimizations: enable chunked streaming with immediate first-token flush; use response chunk sizes tuned to UI (e.g., 64-128 tokens chunks) to keep perceived latency low.

Sample performance/cost estimates (pilot hosted):
- Baseline (redwood-3b-quant, batching + caching): P95 ~ 140-190ms at 150 QPS (depends on prompt distribution).
- If we need tighter P95 (<150ms) we can: reduce batching window (trade cost), increase instance count (higher cost), or use a lower-latency model variant.
- Cost direction: quantized 3B hosted pilot ~40-60% lower $/token vs fp16 7B; reserved capacity usually gives additional 25-40% discount at commit.

Attachments: I attached an SLO-matrix template (SLO-matrix.xlsx) and a short note on cost levers (redwood-cost-levers.pdf). I'll fill the SLO matrix with the numbers from today and send a revised spreadsheet once we run a baseline.

Next steps (suggested):
- You: confirm a 2-week pilot window + preferred start date.
- Us: run a 1-2 day perf baseline (synthetic traffic matching your prompt distribution) and populate the SLO matrix.
- Procurement: we can provide a pilot MSA/quote and reserved-capacity options once we have baseline metrics - estimate 2-3 weeks procurement lead time for standard PO.

Questions for you: can you share representative prompt samples (anonymized) and expected peak hours/days so we can size the pilot?

If helpful, Rishi can join the baseline run to tweak batching/quantization live.

Best,

Alex / Procurement team - quick cost ballpark and next steps below.

Ballpark (hosted pilot, 150 QPS avg, streaming workload, mixed prompt lengths):
- Hosted pilot (metered): ~$18k-$28k / month (depends on actual token volume and cache hit rates).
- Reserved capacity (monthly commit): ~$12k-$20k / month (estimated 25-35% discount at typical commit levels for this footprint).
- Note: enabling aggressive int8 quantization + caching can push costs toward the lower end; using larger fp16 models will be higher.

SLO numbers we expect to validate in baseline (examples):
- redwood-3b-quant (batching + cache): P50 ~ 60-80ms, P95 ~ 140-190ms (streaming first-token latency ~60-110ms).
- redwood-7b (fp16): P50 ~ 40-60ms, P95 ~ 110-150ms but higher $/token.
